title: Secrets and Sensitive Data knowledge check

questions.prompt: What should happen at an external trust boundary?
options: Return secrets in logs to simplify debugging.
Treat incoming data as unknown, validate its structure and policy, then create a trusted domain value.
Cast it to the desired interface and skip validation.
Trust client-submitted roles and ownership fields.
questions.answer_key: Treat incoming data as unknown, validate its structure and policy, then create a trusted domain value.
questions.explanation: Compile-time types do not validate external values or enforce authorization by themselves.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Secrets and Sensitive Data”?
options: The concept should be demonstrated with environment-based configuration and checked against its intended contract.
The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with environment-based configuration and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Environment-based configuration”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Secrets and Sensitive Data”?
options: Assume preventing secrets from entering client bundles and logs is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check secure secret storage, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.answer_key: Check secure secret storage, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Secure secret storage”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
